survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Compass brief uses PIRLS 2016 teacher questionnaire information and reports descriptive percentages of students exposed at least once a week to specific reading activities and teaching practices. The brief does not describe the application of PIRLS complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures, and it does not report any weight variable names. Because the analysis is based on PIRLS International Database outputs and focuses on frequency-based comparisons across education systems, the manuscript provides no explicit guidance on whether analysts should apply student sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or how uncertainty estimates would be computed. For PIRLS microdata users, the standard approach is to apply the provided student sampling weights and replicate weights when producing system-level percentages, but this brief itself does not document that step.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The brief does not analyze cognitive achievement scores with PIRLS plausible values; instead, it reports descriptive frequencies/percentages of students exposed to questionnaire-reported teaching practices and assessment activities. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the reported outcomes. The manuscript also does not document any missing-data strategy for questionnaire items, so missing-data handling cannot be assessed from the text provided.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PIRLS 2016 teacher questionnaire data for education systems where English, French, or German was the main language of instruction. The brief groups systems into English-speaking, German-speaking, and French-speaking categories, and for presentation it reports only selected English-speaking systems (USA, Ontario, Ireland) plus Québec (French-speaking) and Austria and Germany (German-speaking), while noting that other English-speaking systems are available in an online appendix. The analysis is restricted to descriptive statistics (frequencies) for questionnaire items about teaching strategies, reading material types, and assessment/activities, with the reported percentages defined as students exposed at least once a week.

data.outcome_summary: This IEA Compass brief uses PIRLS 2016 teacher questionnaire data to compare how reading literacy is taught across three language-based groups of education systems: English-speaking, German-speaking, and French-speaking. Rather than estimating achievement models, it reports descriptive percentages of students exposed at least once a week to specific reading activities, assessment practices, and types of reading material. Across all groups, traditional surface-level activities (e.g., reading silently/aloud and locating information) are common, while more complex construction/integration tasks (e.g., drawing inferences, making predictions, comparing with experiences) and explicit strategy teaching show substantial between-group differences. English-speaking systems show the highest weekly exposure to complex tasks and explicit strategy instruction, while French-speaking systems—especially Belgium-French—show lower exposure. The brief also highlights assessment practice differences (e.g., interactive talk and written tasks) and notes that Québec often falls between groups, suggesting cultural factors may partially decouple from language-of-instruction categories.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive comparative brief rather than an empirical ML study: it does not train or evaluate predictive models, does not report achievement-score outcomes, and does not provide an analytic sample size or per-country student counts. Consequently, fields such as total_students, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML technique lists are either not applicable or not reported in the provided text. The extraction focuses on the PIRLS 2016 questionnaire-based frequency comparisons across selected education systems.
